title: Irreducible-closed intervals across two overlapping open subspaces
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, and let $U,V\subseteq X$ be open subsets, all subsets carrying their subspace topologies [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Let $Z\subseteq Z'$ be irreducible closed subsets of $V$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], and assume $Z\cap U\ne\varnothing$. Put $W=U\cap V$, $C=\overline{Z\cap W}^{\,U}$, and $C'=\overline{Z'\cap W}^{\,U}$, where the superscript specifies the ambient space of closure. Then $C\subseteq C'$ are irreducible closed subsets of $U$, with $C\cap W=Z\cap W$ and $C'\cap W=Z'\cap W$. Define $[Z,Z']_V$ to be all irreducible closed subsets $D$ of $V$ with $Z\subseteq D\subseteq Z'$, ordered by inclusion, and define $[C,C']_U$ analogously. The formulas $F(D)=\overline{D\cap W}^{\,U}$ and $G(E)=\overline{E\cap W}^{\,V}$ define inverse inclusion-preserving bijections $F:[Z,Z']_V\longrightarrow[C,C']_U$ and $G:[C,C']_U\longrightarrow[Z,Z']_V$, taking endpoints to endpoints. They identify each of these entire intervals with the interval of irreducible closed subsets of $W$ between $Z\cap W$ and $Z'\cap W$, by intersection with $W$. They induce length-preserving inverse bijections on finite strict chains with these endpoints, and on saturated chains with these endpoints. Length means number of strict inclusions; saturated means no irreducible closed subset can be inserted between two adjacent members. Thus the two intervals have the same attainable strict-chain lengths and the same attainable saturated-chain lengths. No affineness, separation, sobriety, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $X,U,V,W$.

source.place: Tag 02I2 (lemma-catenary), restriction/closure correspondence in the proof, applied to W inside V and inside U and restricted to the full endpoint intervals.

proof.text: By [def-kun-subspace-topology], $W=U\cap V$ is open both in $U$ and in $V$, and either iterated subspace topology on $W$ has opens $O\cap W$ for $O$ open in $X$. Set $A=Z\cap W$ and $B=Z'\cap W$. Since $Z\subseteq V$, $Z\cap U=A\ne\varnothing$; also $B\supseteq A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] to $W\subseteq V$: $A\subseteq B$ are irreducible closed in $W$, with closures $Z,Z'$ in $V$. Apply its inverse for $W\subseteq U$: their closures $C\subseteq C'$ are irreducible closed in $U$, and $C\cap W=A$, $C'\cap W=B$.

source.place: Tag 02I2 (lemma-catenary), proof: restriction/closure bijection; details of the endpoint intervals and chains supplied here.

proof.text: Let $J$ consist of the irreducible closed subsets $T$ of $W$ with $A\subseteq T\subseteq B$. The correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] for $W\subseteq V$ restricts to $r_V:[Z,Z']_V\to J$, $D\mapsto D\cap W$. Every such $D$ meets $W$ since it contains $Z$, and its intersection lies between $A,B$. Conversely $s_V(T)=\overline T^{\,V}$ lies between $\overline A^{\,V}=Z$ and $\overline B^{\,V}=Z'$. The cited inverse identities give $s_V(r_V(D))=D$ and $r_V(s_V(T))=T$ for every $D,T$ in these full intervals. Both maps preserve inclusion.

source.place: Tag 02I2 (lemma-catenary), proof: restriction/closure bijection; details of the endpoint intervals and chains supplied here.

proof.text: For $W\subseteq U$, [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] likewise restricts to $r_U:[C,C']_U\to J$ with inverse $s_U(T)=\overline T^{\,U}$. Every $E$ in this interval meets $W$ since $E\supseteq C$ and $C\cap W=A\ne\varnothing$; conversely closure in $U$ sends $A\subseteq T\subseteq B$ into $C\subseteq s_U(T)\subseteq C'$. The cited inverse identities give $s_U(r_U(E))=E$ and $r_U(s_U(T))=T$ on these full intervals. Hence $F=s_Ur_V$ and $G=s_Vr_U$ have the asserted formulas, with $F(D)\cap W=D\cap W$ and $G(E)\cap W=E\cap W$. Explicitly $GF=s_Vr_Us_Ur_V=s_Vr_V=1$ and $FG=s_Ur_Vs_Vr_U=s_Ur_U=1$. Both preserve inclusion; $F(Z)=C$, $F(Z')=C'$ and the inverse identities give the reverse endpoint equalities.

source.place: Tag 02I2 (lemma-catenary), proof: restriction/closure bijection; details of the endpoint intervals and chains supplied here.

proof.text: For a finite strict chain $Z=D_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq D_n=Z'$, apply $F$ termwise. Inclusion is preserved, and equality of two images would give equality of the original terms after applying $G$. Hence the image is a strict chain from $C$ to $C'$ with exactly $n$ inclusions. Termwise $G$ reverses this construction, giving inverse length-preserving bijections, including the one-term chains when the endpoints coincide.

source.place: Tag 02I2 (lemma-catenary), proof: restriction/closure bijection; details of the endpoint intervals and chains supplied here.

proof.text: An insertion $F(D_i)\subsetneq E\subsetneq F(D_{i+1})$ automatically lies in $[C,C']_U$ and yields $D_i\subsetneq G(E)\subsetneq D_{i+1}$ by the inverse inclusion-preserving bijection. Conversely any insertion between $D_i,D_{i+1}$ maps by $F$ to an insertion between their images. Thus a chain has no allowable insertion exactly when its image has none. Restricting the preceding inverse chain maps gives the asserted saturated-chain bijections and equality of attainable lengths. The adjacency argument also applies if chains with other index sets are allowed. All applications used only openness and the stated nonempty intersection.
